newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel - Europe needs more than "village currencies".
newsitem.headline: Kinkel - Europe needs more than "village currencies".

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel introduced a new term into the debate about Europe's single currency on Tuesday with a warning the EU could not compete in world trade if it only had "village currencies."
But the often blunt minister was careful not to repeat negative remarks his colleagues have made about European currencies they say are less stable than the deutschemark.
Arguing for the Euro, Kinkel said even the mark would be a "village currency" in 10 years compared to the U.S. dollar and the Japanese yen because of their dominant role in world trade.
"I'm convinced we need the Euro," he told journalists in Bonn. "Europe can't continue to be competitive with village currencies."

Kinkel admitted his new term -- "Dorfwaehrungen" in German -- was a bit exaggerated but said it brought the message home to average Germans attending pro-Euro discussion evenings he has addressed recently.
Germany has been one of the strongest proponents of the Euro, which is due to be launched in 1999, but popular doubts about losing the mark are still strong.
